steps.text: Place 1 chicken breast between 2 sheets of plastic wrap or parchment paper on a cutting board. Using a meat mallet or a rolling pin, gently pound each breast to 1/2-inch thickness. Repeat with remaining chicken breasts.

Place lemon juice, olive oil, dried oregano, seasoning salt, black pepper, and onion powder into a large zip-top bag; squeeze to combine marinade. Add chicken and press out as much air as possible before sealing the bag. Gently massage chicken to distribute marinade. Marinate chicken in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes or up to 12 hours.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.

Remove chicken from marinade and place, smooth-side down, on the preheated grill; cook, covered, until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, about 5 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of chicken breast should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Discard excess marinade.
Transfer chicken to a cutting board and tent with aluminum foil. Let rest for 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Juicy Grilled Chicken Breasts
raw_recipe.description: This delicious grilled chicken breast gets a flavor boost from a simple lemon and oregano marinade before cooking on the grill until golden and juicy.

review.reviewBody: A new family favorite! I let the chicken breasts soak while I heated up the grill - about 5 minutes - then seasoned with garlic powder, seasoned salt and Italian herb seasoning. I turned the heat down to medium low and cooked them "low and slow" - about 6 minutes on one side, 10 minutes on the other. When I turned the breasts, I put a pat of butter on each to keep things moist. The results were outstanding. Nothing plain or run-of-the-mill about it! The ckicken was bursting with flavor - you could taste the lemon juice as well as the seasonings. The only thing I will do differently next time is double the amount of chicken cooked. My husband is disappointed there isn't more for leftovers!
My family really enjoyed this. I put the ingredients in my frozen bag of chicken and let it marinate while it was thawing. Next time I would add seasoned pepper and maybe some garlic. Very good.

Really easy and tasty, even my 9 year old was asking to try it, foregoing her mac n cheese. Paired well with "Skewered Grilled Potatoes" for an all on the grill meal that was pretty fast and used mostly pantry items. Only mod was I used tenders as my wife likes them better. Pellet grill was set to 425, cooked about 5 mins per side until IT was 150, then put on the cold side while potatoes finished.

I've been wanting to try this for a while because of how simple it is.. And I love lemon and chicken. I opted to use 3 garlic cloves minced instead of the onion powder and used Oregano in place of parsley. Also used to zest of the lemon. I pounded my chicken breasts to about twice the size and marinated them for 1 hour(drizzled in about 2 tbsp of olive oil also.
I enjoyed the overall light flavor of this.
I don't see how just dipping the chicken quickly in the lemon juice absorbs any of the flavours.. Seems like a waste to me... But I like a lot of flavor. 
I didn't end up having any juices to discard after an hour of marinated.. Because it all stuck on the chicken.. Perhaps would of rated lower if I followed the method.
Highly recommended marinating for optimal flavors. Don't marinate more than 2 hours as the lemon juice will start to cook the chicken.
Our grill ended up not working, so I pan-fried these using olive oil and butter. They were super delicious! I’ll definitely put this in our dinner rotation.

Super easy to make! The prep time is even less than 15 minutes. The one thing I specifically note is the “seasoning salt.” Most people immediately think of Lawry’s but my wife has Celiac’s and even though there’s nothing on the label that should affect her, it does! All the Celiac forums report the same issue. I used “Jane’s Krazy Mixed Up” and she has no issues. Overall a delicious recipe!

Used less lemon juice (only juice of one lemon), mixed all ingredients and marinated chicken for a few hours before searing in a cast iron skillet and finishing in the oven. They were delicious. Glad I used less lemon when marinating as the lemon taste was enough. Great easy recipe.

Good enough for company. Made it twice so far. Today made it for company and everyone raved. I cut my chicken breasts in half to make them a little thinner. Marinated them in the lemon juice for 15 - 30 min and for the seasoned salt I used the McCormick Grill Mates Smoke House Maple. I used the onion powder, salt and pepper as called for. I also used the butter pats while grilling as recommended by Trinka. Do not overcook!! I cooked approx 9 minutes total and could have even gone less time on the thinner pieces. It was delicious.

Delicious and juicy. I added some thyme and rosemary to the lemon juice n spice mix and let it soak for 10 mins, seasoned with salt/pepper while on the grill, and brushed on some olive oil a few minutes before taking off. Went perfectly with a linguine aglio e olio.

this was awesome!!! I did the oregano and cilantro version cutting a pocket in the chicken and inserting the cilantro and sliced garlic. i also baked it in oven because it too cold to grille right now.. i will absolutely make this again

I've been 'qing for45+ years and I don't use recipes that do not provide specific temperatures for the process. I made this last night on my Weber Kettle grill and it never cooked through. The "medium" temperature instruction is useless as is the time. The thermometer on my kettle only goes to 500° (F) so medium for that would be 250. I cooked the chicken at 250 for 5 minutes per side as per the recipe. The outside of the meat was burned to a crisp and the inside was raw. Seriously, it is time to get away from non-numerical temps in recipes when grills have them built in, many ovens do, too, and there are more thermometers for cooking than you can shake a wok ladle at.

These got devoured before I got a picture. I bought thin butterflied chicken breasts and skipped the beating! I used concentrated lemon juice. I marinated in a casserole dish for about 5 hours in the fridge while I went on with my day. I'm adding this to one of my favorites! Super easy and practically fool proof. Great with egg noodles and broccoli.
Followed instructions as written. Perfect! Chicken was nicely charred on outside, very moist on the inside. Definite keeper.
Simple enough and makes a tender, tasty breast.
I used marjoram instead of oregano.
Delicious! Will be part of the rotation.

Too much lemon juice for me.

We liked it and i did follow the added suggestions of a pad of butter on each piece after you turn them - came out great and I even handled the grill! Burned my arm but really enjoyed the chicken! Thanks for a great recipe.
Marinade was quite tart, I added teaspoon of sugar to offset tartness of lemon.
